problem: Prior neural graph models aggregate a node's neighbourhood with fixed, structure-given weights (GCN gives every node of a neighbourhood the same importance), need costly matrix operations or upfront access to the whole graph structure, or sample a fixed-size, ordered neighbourhood (GraphSAGE-LSTM). A layer is needed that weighs each neighbour by its own learned importance, computed from node features only, over the entire unordered neighbourhood.

inputs: node features h_i, h_j ∈ R^F (all nodes of the neighbourhood)
the neighbourhood N_i of node i (first-order neighbours including i): the graph structure, used only as a mask
outputs: new node features h'_i: ∈ R^{KF'} on hidden layers (K heads concatenated) or ∈ R^{F'} on the final (prediction) layer (K heads averaged, then σ)

contributions.name: masked attention: attention coefficients α_ij over j ∈ N_i
contributions.solves: GCN-style aggregation assigns every node of a neighbourhood the same fixed weight; GAT lets each neighbour j get its own learned importance α_ij, computed from the features W h_i and W h_j (Sec. 2.2: 'assigning different importances to nodes of a same neighborhood').
contributions.shown_by: the attention band along the top: W h_i ‖ W h_j → aᵀ (accent) → LeakyReLU → e_ij → softmax_j → the accent α_ij strip (one cell per node of the 5-node neighbourhood glyph), with the note 'masked attention: a learned α_ij per j, not a fixed weight'; the graph enters only through the grey control edge 'only j ∈ N_i' into the pair concatenation

contributions.name: graph attentional layer: attention-weighted aggregation shared by all edges
contributions.solves: no eigendecompositions or upfront access to the global graph structure; works on the entire neighbourhood without assuming an order (Sec. 2.2), so it applies to inductive tasks
contributions.shown_by: one weighted sum Σ_j α_ij W h_j fed by the shared linear map W (W h_j along the main line) and by the α_ij strip from above, inside the frame named 'Graph attentional layer'

contributions.name: multi-head attention: K heads concatenated or averaged
contributions.solves: stabilises the learning process of self-attention (Sec. 2.1)
contributions.shown_by: frame title 'K independent heads, one shown'; one strip 'heads 2…K' (the other heads' weighted sums) feeds both combinations: through σ into the head concatenation (©) next to this head's σ(Σ_j α_ij W h_j), giving h'_i ∈ R^{KF'} (4 cells, hidden layers); and directly into Mean_k next to this head's sum, then σ gives h'_i ∈ R^{F'} (2 cells, final layer)

mechanism.explains: how one head computes α_ij: the shared W maps h_i and h_j, the pair W h_i ‖ W h_j (only for j ∈ N_i) is projected by aᵀ, LeakyReLU gives e_ij, and a softmax over j ∈ N_i normalises it to α_ij
how α_ij is used: it weights the sum Σ_j α_ij W h_j; σ follows, and the K heads are concatenated (hidden layers) or averaged before the final σ (output layer)

color_semantics.blue: node feature vectors: h_i, h_j, the other heads' outputs and h'_i (white cells in editorial-minimal)
color_semantics.gray: reused operations (W, LeakyReLU, softmax, weighted sum, mean) and the input graph
color_semantics.teal: GAT's attention, the contribution: the vector a and the coefficients α_ij it produces, plus the band note (the editorial-minimal accent; the legend's 'proposed (ours)' swatch)

annotate: h_i, h_j on the input strip
W h_i, W h_j on the W → ‖ edge and W h_j on the main line
e_ij on the LeakyReLU → softmax edge
σ on the edges into the head concatenation and after Mean_k
h'_i ∈ R^{KF'} (hidden) and h'_i ∈ R^{F'} (output) under the output strips
only j ∈ N_i on the grey control edge from the graph glyph
heads 2…K on the one strip entering © (through σ) and Mean_k
takeaway: For node i, each GAT head scores every neighbour j ∈ N_i from the pair (W h_i, W h_j) — aᵀ, LeakyReLU, softmax over N_i — and uses these attention coefficients α_ij to weight the sum of W h_j; K such heads are concatenated (hidden layers) or averaged (output layer) to give h'_i.

reader_questions.glance: Node features and the neighbourhood of node i go in; a weighted sum over the neighbours gives h'_i.
reader_questions.detail: The weights α_ij come from aᵀ[W h_i ‖ W h_j], LeakyReLU and a softmax restricted to N_i; K heads are concatenated or averaged.

why: The 2-minute reader needs both how α_ij is computed (Eqs. 1–3) and how it weights the sum and combines across heads (Eqs. 4–6). HGT's attention band stacked above the aggregation line shows both in one left-to-right reading and fits the 5.5 in ICLR text width at the 7 pt floor. The Equiformer stack (c2) is the right grammar but would print about as tall as it is wide at this width; the HAN star (c3) shows the weighted aggregation but hides how α_ij is computed, and the graph glyph cannot write α on its individual edges.
highlight: The figure is the expanded graph attentional layer: a white frame named in its bold title, which also says K independent heads, one shown. Inside it only GAT's attention — aᵀ and the α_ij strip, plus the band note — carries the accent; reused operations are light grey boxes and feature vectors white cells. Bold labels and the dark accent outline (not hue alone) mark the accent in a grayscale print.

data_visuals.what: input neighbourhood: node i (centre) and its first-order neighbours N_i — a schematic toy graph, not a dataset sample
node feature vectors h_i, h_j ∈ R^F as a short strip of cells
attention coefficients α_ij, one cell per node of the 5-node neighbourhood glyph (including i)
output features h'_i: 4 cells (K heads × F' concatenated) on hidden layers, 2 cells (F', averaged) on the output layer
weighted sums of the other heads (k = 2…K), one 2-cell feature strip entering the concatenation (through σ) and the mean

drawn_as.how: the attention mechanism a (Eq. 1) is drawn as its expanded form (Eq. 3): concatenation, the weight vector aᵀ and LeakyReLU
masked attention is the 'j ∈ N_i' edge from the neighbourhood glyph into the pair concatenation: e_ij is computed only for j ∈ N_i
the per-head nonlinearity σ of Eq. 4 is the label σ on the edge from the weighted sum into the head concatenation
the final nonlinearity σ of Eq. 6, applied after averaging, is the label σ on the edge from Mean_k to the output strip
h' is drawn twice: concatenated (KF' features, hidden layers) and averaged (F' features, final layer)
